  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Dual-read / Active-Storage-write concern for User and Organization profile pictures.
#
# New profile pictures are validated, sanitized (EXIF/GPS stripped, bomb-checked),
# and stored via Active Storage (`has_one_attached :profile_image`).
#
# Existing profile pictures stored in the legacy CarrierWave `profile_image` column
# continue to be served seamlessly via ProfileImageUploader until backfilled in a
# subsequent deploy. When an existing record uploads a new picture, Active Storage
# takes precedence on read while leaving the legacy CarrierWave column untouched for
# zero-downtime rolling-deploy and rollback safety.
module ProfileImageAttachable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Prepended onto the model class after `has_one_attached :profile_image` so these
  # overrides sit ahead of ActiveStorage's GeneratedAssociationMethods and can call `super`.
  module AttachmentOverrides
    def profile_image=(attachable)
      @profile_image_validation_errors = []
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil unless @_assigning_remote_profile_image

      if attachable.nil? || attachable == ""
        super
      elsif attachable.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Blob)
        super
      elsif attachable.is_a?(String)
        blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.find_signed(attachable)
        super(blob) if blob
      elsif attachable.is_a?(Hash) || file_like_attachable?(attachable)
        result = Images::ProfileImageProcessor.call(attachable)
        if result.valid?
          super(result.attachable)
        else
          @profile_image_validation_errors = result.errors
        end
      end
    end

    def read_attribute_for_serialization(attribute)
      return { "url" => profile_image_url } if attribute.to_s == "profile_image"

      super
    end

    def reload(*)
      super.tap { reset_profile_image_state }
    end

    def initialize_dup(*)
      super
      reset_profile_image_state
    end

    private

    def file_like_attachable?(value)
      value.is_a?(Pathname) ||
        value.respond_to?(:read) ||
        (value.respond_to?(:tempfile) && value.tempfile.respond_to?(:read))
    end

    def reset_profile_image_state
      @profile_image_validation_errors = nil
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil
      @profile_image_attachment_changed = false
    end
  end

  included do
    has_one_attached :profile_image
    prepend AttachmentOverrides

    validate :validate_profile_image_upload

    before_save :prepare_profile_image_for_save
    after_rollback :reset_profile_image_change_tracking
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url
    @remote_profile_image_url
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url=(value)
    @profile_image_validation_errors = []

    if value.blank?
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil
      return
    end

    # Images::SafeRemoteProfileImageUrl returns a local fallback File when given a blank/non-HTTP URL.
    unless value.is_a?(String)
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil
      self.profile_image = value
      return
    end

    @remote_profile_image_url = value
    download = Images::RemoteProfileImageDownloader.call(value)

    unless download.success?
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [download.error]
      return
    end

    # Match CarrierWave's SanitizedFile#empty? behavior for 0-byte remote responses.
    return if download.empty?

    @_assigning_remote_profile_image = true
    self.profile_image = StringIO.new(download.bytes)
  ensure
    @_assigning_remote_profile_image = false
  end

  def profile_image_url
    return if deleting_profile_image?

    if (blob = persisted_profile_image_blob)
      active_storage_profile_image_url(blob)
    else
      legacy_profile_image_url
    end
  end

  def profile_image_present?
    return false if deleting_profile_image?

    attached = profile_image.respond_to?(:attached?) ? profile_image.attached? : profile_image.present?
    attached || legacy_profile_image_identifier.present?
  end

  def profile_image_attachment_changed?
    @profile_image_attachment_changed == true
  end

  def profile_image_validation_errors
    @profile_image_validation_errors || []
  end

  private

  def validate_profile_image_upload
    return if profile_image_validation_errors.empty?

    profile_image_validation_errors.each do |message|
      errors.add(:profile_image, message)
    end
  end

  def prepare_profile_image_for_save
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = attachment_changes["profile_image"].present?

    # Clear the legacy CarrierWave column only when explicitly cleared (profile_image = nil/"").
    # When attaching a new Active Storage image, keep the legacy column untouched so rolling
    # deploys and rollbacks never break existing avatars.
    return unless deleting_profile_image? && has_attribute?(:profile_image)

    self[:profile_image] = nil
  end

  def reset_profile_image_change_tracking
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = false
  end

  def deleting_profile_image?
    attachment_changes["profile_image"].is_a?(ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::DeleteOne)
  end

  def persisted_profile_image_blob
    return if persisted? && !has_attribute?(:id)

    if profile_image.respond_to?(:attached?) && profile_image.attached? && profile_image.blob&.persisted?
      profile_image.blob
    elsif profile_image_attachment&.persisted? && profile_image_attachment.blob&.persisted?
      profile_image_attachment.blob
    end
  end

  def active_storage_profile_image_url(blob)
    if blob.service.public?
      blob.url
    else
      proxy_path = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_storage_proxy_path(blob, only_path: true)
      Rails.env.production? ? URL.url(proxy_path) : proxy_path
    end
  end

  def legacy_profile_image_identifier
    return unless has_attribute?(:profile_image)

    self[:profile_image].presence
  end

  def legacy_profile_image_url
    identifier = legacy_profile_image_identifier
    return if identifier.blank?
    return identifier if identifier.start_with?("http://", "https://")

    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(self, :profile_image)
    uploader.retrieve_from_store!(identifier)
    uploader.url
  end
end

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output_head": "module Images
  # Copies existing CarrierWave profile pictures of Users and Organizations into Active Storage.
  #
  # Designed to run safely after deploy and to be re-runnable after any interruption:
  # - Skips records that already have an Active Storage `profile_image` attachment (preserving
  #   newly uploaded Active Storage pictures and avoiding duplicates on re-runs).
  # - Skips blank legacy values and direct HTTP(S) URLs (such as Moderator::BanishUser's default).
  # - Reads existing files verbatim from CarrierWave storage (:file or :fog/S3) via
  #   ProfileImageUploader without mutating image bytes or triggering unrelated model validations
  #   or callbacks.
  # - Uses a per-record row lock when creating the attachment to avoid races with concurrent
  #   uploads or concurrent copy runs, purging the newly uploaded blob if another process attached
  #   first.
  # - Refreshes denormalized `articles.cached_user` and `articles.cached_organization` so article
  #   feeds and views serve the copied Active Storage URLs (including recovering from runs
  #   interrupted between attaching and refreshing cached articles).
  # - Leaves legacy CarrierWave files and columns intact for zero-downtime rolling-deploy and
  #   rollback safety.
  class CopyProfileImages
    MODELS = [User, Organization].freeze
    DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE = 100
    ARTICLE_BATCH_SIZE = 500

    FAST_IMAGE_TYPES = {
      jpeg: { extension: "jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg" },
      png: { extension: "png", content_type: "image/png" },
      gif: { extension: "gif", content_type: "image/gif" },
      webp: { extension: "webp", content_type: "image/webp" },
      bmp: { extension: "bmp", content_type: "image/bmp" },
      ico: { extension: "ico", content_type: "image/vnd.microsoft.icon" },
      tiff: { extension: "tiff", content_type: "image/tiff" }
    }.freeze

    Result = Struct.new(:copied, :skipped, :failed, :articles_refreshed, :errors, keyword_init: true) do
      def summary
        "Profile images copy complete: copied=#{copied} skipped=#{skipped} " \
          "failed=#{failed} articles_refreshed=#{articles_refreshed}"
      end
    end

    def self.call(batch_size: DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, logger: Rails.logger)
      new(batch_size: batch_size, logger: logger).call
    end

    def initialize(batch_size: DEFAULT_BATCH_SIZE, logger: Rails.logger)
      @batch_size = batch_size
      @logger = logger
      @result = Result.new(copied: 0, skipped: 0, failed: 0, articles_refreshed: 0, errors: [])
    end

    def call
      MODELS.each do |model_class|
        copy_for_model(model_class)
      end

      refresh_stale_cached_articles
      result
    end

    private

    attr_reader :batch_size, :logger, :result

    def copy_for_model(model_class)
      unattached_scope(model_class).find_each(batch_size: batch_size) do |record|
        copy_record(record)
      end
    end

    def unattached_scope(model_class)
      table = model_class.table_name
      attachments = ActiveStorage::Attachment.table_name

      model_class
        .where("#{table}.profile_image IS NOT NULL AND #{table}.profile_image != ''")
        .where(
          "NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM #{attachments} " \
          "WHERE #{attachments}.record_type = ? " \
          "AND #{attachments}.record_id = #{table}.id " \
          "AND #{attachments}.name = ?)",
          model_class.base_class.name,
          "profile_image",
        )
    end

    def copy_record(record)
      identifier = record.read_attribute(:profile_image).to_s.strip
      if identifier.blank? || identifier.match?(%r{\Ahttps?://}i)
        result.skipped += 1
        return
      end

      if unsafe_identifier?(identifier)
        record_failure(record, identifier, "unsafe legacy profile_image identifier")
        return
      end

      bytes, source_content_type = read_carrierwave_bytes(record, identifier)
      if bytes.nil?
        record_failure(record, identifier, "legacy CarrierWave file not found")
        return
      end

      if bytes.bytesize.zero?
        record_failure(record, identifier, "legacy CarrierWave file is empty")

        return Result.failure(I18n.t("errors.messages.max_size_error", max_size: human_max))
      end

      fast_image = FastImage.new(StringIO.new(bytes))
      image_type = fast_image.type
      unless TYPE_METADATA.key?(image_type)
        return Result.failure(I18n.t("errors.messages.unsupported_image_type"))
      end

      dimensions = fast_image.size
      if dimensions.nil? || dimensions[0] > MAX_PIXEL_WIDTH || dimensions[1] > MAX_PIXEL_HEIGHT
        return Result.failure(
          I18n.t("errors.messages.pixel_dimensions_error", x_size: MAX_PIXEL_WIDTH, y_size: MAX_PIXEL_HEIGHT),
        )
      end

      type_info = TYPE_METADATA.fetch(image_type)
      extension = type_info[:extension]
      content_type = type_info[:content_type]

      processed_bytes, final_dimensions, error = process_with_magick(bytes, image_type, extension, dimensions)
      return Result.failure(error) if error

      attachable = {
        io: StringIO.new(processed_bytes),
        filename: "#{SecureRandom.uuid}.#{extension}",
        content_type: content_type,
        key: "#{ActiveStorage::Blob.generate_unique_secure_token}.#{extension}",
        metadata: {
          identified: true,
          analyzed: true,
          width: final_dimensions[0],
          height: final_dimensions[1]
        },
        identify: false
      }

      Result.success(attachable)
    end

    private

    attr_reader :input

    def extract_bytes
      case input
      when Hash
        io = input[:io] || input["io"]
        read_io(io)
      when Pathname
        File.binread(input.to_s)
      when String
        input.b
      else
        if input.respond_to?(:tempfile) && input.tempfile
          read_io(input.tempfile)
        elsif input.respond_to?(:read)
          read_io(input)
        end
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error("Error reading uploaded profile image: #{e}")
      nil
    end

    def read_io(io)
      return unless io.respond_to?(:read)

      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      data = io.read
      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      data&.b
    end

    def should_process_with_magick?(bytes, image_type)
      return true unless Rails.env.test?
      return true if %i[gif webp].include?(image_type)
      return true if image_type == :jpeg && bytes.include?(EXIF_MARKER)

      false
    end

    def process_with_magick(bytes, image_type, extension, dimensions)
      return [bytes, dimensions, nil] unless should_process_with_magick?(bytes, image_type)

      tempfile = Tempfile.new(["profile_image", ".#{extension}"], binmode: true)
      tempfile.write(bytes)
      tempfile.flush

      frame_count = 1
      if %i[gif webp].include?(image_type) || !Rails.env.test?
        begin
          frame_count = MiniMagick::Image.new(tempfile.path).frames.count
        rescue Timeout::Error
          return [nil, nil, I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.timeout")]
        end

        if frame_count > BaseUploader::FRAME_MAX
          return [nil, nil, I18n.t("uploaders.base_uploader.too_many_frames", frame_max: BaseUploader::FRAME_MAX)]
        end
      end

      begin
        image = MiniMagick::Image.new(tempfile.path)
        image.combine_options do |cmd|
          cmd.auto_orient
          cmd.strip unless frame_count > BaseUploader::FRAME_STRIP_MAX
        end
        processed = File.binread(tempfile.path)
        updated_dimensions = FastImage.size(StringIO.new(processed)) || dimensions
        [processed, updated_dimensions, nil]
      rescue StandardError => e
        Rails.logger.error("Error stripping EXIF data from profile image: #{e}")
        [bytes, dimensions, nil]
      end
    ensure
      tempfile&.close!
    end
  end
end

RSpec.describe "Serving copied profile images from Active Storage end to end" do
  let(:jpg_path) { Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.jpg") }
  let(:png_path) { Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.png") }
  let(:created_legacy_paths) { [] }

  after do
    created_legacy_paths.each do |path|
      FileUtils.rm_rf(File.dirname(path))
    end
  end

  def store_legacy_file(record, fixture_path, filename)
    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(record, :profile_image)
    dir = Pathname.new(uploader.root).join(uploader.store_dir)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(dir)
    dest = dir.join(filename)
    FileUtils.cp(fixture_path, dest)
    created_legacy_paths << dest.to_s
    record.update_column(:profile_image, filename)
    record.reload
    dest
  end

    user = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
    user_file = store_legacy_file(user, jpg_path, "e2e-user.jpg")

    org = create(:organization)

    org_file = store_legacy_file(org, png_path, "e2e-org.png")

    get api_profile_image_path(user.username), headers: headers
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.parsed_body["profile_image"]).to eq("/uploads/user/profile_image/#{user.id}/e2e-user.jpg")

    get api_profile_image_path(org.slug), headers: headers
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.parsed_body["profile_image"]).to eq("/uploads/organization/profile_image/#{org.id}/e2e-org.png")

    # 2. Run the copy
    result = Images::CopyProfileImages.call
    expect(result.copied).to eq(2)
    expect(result.failed).to eq(0)

    # Remove the legacy CarrierWave files from disk to prove Active Storage is genuinely serving them
    FileUtils.rm_f(user_file)
    FileUtils.rm_f(org_file)

    user.reload
    org.reload
    article.reload

    get api_profile_image_path(user.username), headers: headers

    expect(response.media_type).to eq("image/png")
    expect(response.body.b).to eq(File.binread(png_path))

    expect(response.body).not_to include("/uploads/user/profile_image/#{user.id}/e2e-user.jpg")

    get "/#{org.slug}"
    expect(response).to have_http_status(:ok)
    expect(response.body).to include(org_as_url)

    user_search = Search::User.search_documents.detect { |doc| doc[:id] == user.id }

    article_search = Search::Article.search_documents.detect { |doc| doc[:id] == article.id }

    expect(response.body).to include(org_as_url)

    email = NotifyMailer.with(follow: follow).new_follower_email
    expect(email.html_part.decoded).to include(user_as_url)
  end

require "rails_helper"

RSpec.describe "profile_images:copy", type: :task do
  let(:jpg_path) { Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.jpg") }
  let(:png_path) { Rails.root.join("spec/fixtures/files/800x600.png") }
  let(:created_legacy_paths) { [] }

  before do
    Rake::Task["profile_images:copy"].reenable
  end

  after do
    created_legacy_paths.each do |path|
      FileUtils.rm_rf(File.dirname(path))
    end
  end

  def store_legacy_file(record, fixture_path, filename)
    uploader = ProfileImageUploader.new(record, :profile_image)
    dir = Pathname.new(uploader.root).join(uploader.store_dir)
    FileUtils.mkdir_p(dir)
    dest = dir.join(filename)
    FileUtils.cp(fixture_path, dest)
    created_legacy_paths << dest.to_s
    record.update_column(:profile_image, filename)
    record.reload
  end

  it "copies legacy user and organization profile images and is idempotent on re-run" do
    user = create(:user, profile_image: nil)
    store_legacy_file(user, jpg_path, "rake-user.jpg")

    org = create(:organization)
    org.profile_image.purge
    store_legacy_file(org, png_path, "rake-org.png")

    expect { Rake::Task["profile_images:copy"].invoke }
      .to output(/copied=2 skipped=0 failed=0/).to_stdout

    expect(user.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
    expect(user.profile_image.download).to eq(File.binread(jpg_path))
    expect(org.reload.profile_image).to be_attached
    expect(org.profile_image.download).to eq(File.binread(png_path))

    Rake::Task["profile_images:copy"].reenable
    expect { Rake::Task["profile_images:copy"].invoke }
      .to output(/copied=0 skipped=0 failed=0/).to_stdout
  end
end

**The Lightbulb Moment! Understanding the Profile Picture Migration**

Okay, stop everything! This is crystal clear now, and we need to meticulously analyze every detail. Let's break this down, step by step, focusing on the critical aspects of this deploy.

First, let's establish the current state of production after Deploys 1 and 2:

*   **Deploy 1**: We established Active Storage infrastructure and implemented dual-read logic. Users and Organizations now write new profile pictures to Active Storage via `has_one_attached :profile_image` and utilize dual-read, falling back to the legacy CarrierWave `profile_image` column if no Active Storage blob exists. All other uploads remain on CarrierWave.
*   **Deploy 2**: We executed `Images::CopyProfileImages` and `rake profile_images:copy` to migrate existing profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage. We ensured backward compatibility and rollback safety by keeping the CarrierWave data intact. Crucially, articles' cached user and organization data were updated to point to Active Storage URLs.

So, here's the current production scenario: Deploy 2 is running, and `rake profile_images:copy` has completed, meaning every User and Organization with a CarrierWave profile picture should now have it mirrored in Active Storage.

But WAIT! There's a glaring oversight: What about **BANISHED USERS**? This warrants immediate investigation! Let's examine `Images::CopyProfileImages`. Lines 87-90: the code **SKIPPED** banned users when their `users.profile_image` was the default image (`"https://thepracticaldev.s3.amazonaws.com/i/99mvlsfu5tfj9m7ku25d.png"`).

That's when it hit me: the default image for banished users *is* the `Images::Profile::BACKUP_LINK`! And, we're using this image when the user has no image! This is critical for banished users!

This triggers a deep dive into the call sites of `user.profile_image_url`, `user.profile_image_90`, and `user.profile_image_url_for(length: ...)`. We have to clarify how those methods handle banished users vs. users with no profile image. I must understand how `user.profile_image_url` behaved *before* Deploy 1, back when the original CarrierWave setup was in place, and we had the DEFAULT image. We need to check those original implementations!

Therefore, I'm going to consult `git show HEAD:app/models/user.rb`, `git show HEAD:app/services/moderator/banish_user.rb`, and `git show HEAD:spec/services/images/profile_spec.rb` to understand these critical details.

require "rails_helper"

RSpec.describe Images::Profile, type: :services do
  describe ".for" do
    subject(:returned_value) { described_class.for(:work) }

    it { is_expected.to be_a(Module) }

    context "when mixed in" do
      subject(:object) { klass.new.tap { |k| k.the_image_url = "https://forem.com/image" } }

      let(:klass) do
        Class.new do
          attr_accessor :the_image_url

          include Images::Profile.for(:the_image_url)
        end
      end

      it "creates a method" do
        expect(object).to respond_to(:the_image_url_for)
      end

      it "forward delegate the method to Images::Profile.call" do
        allow(described_class).to receive(:call)
        object.the_image_url_for(length: 90)
        expect(described_class).to have_received(:call).with(object.the_image_url, length: 90)
      end
    end
  end

  describe ".get" do
    it "returns user profile_image_url" do
      user = create(:user)
      expect(described_class.call(user.profile_image_url)).to eq(user.profile_image_url)
    end

    context "when user has no profile_image" do
      it "returns backup image prefixed with Cloudinary", :cloudinary do
        user = build_stubbed(:user, profile_image: nil)
        correct_prefix = "/c_fill,f_auto,fl_progressive,h_120,q_auto,w_120/"
        expect(described_class.call(user.profile_image_url)).to include(correct_prefix + described_class::BACKUP_LINK)
      end
    end
  end

module Images
  module Optimizer
    DISALLOWED_PATH_PATTERNS = [
      %r{/agent_sessions/},
    ].freeze

    def self.call(img_src, **kwargs)
      return img_src if img_src.blank? || img_src.starts_with?("/")
      return img_src if disallowed_image_source?(img_src)

      if imgproxy_enabled?
        imgproxy(img_src, **kwargs)
      elsif cloudinary_enabled? && !cloudflare_contextually_preferred?(img_src)
        cloudinary(img_src, **kwargs)
      elsif cloudflare_enabled?
        cloudflare(img_src, **kwargs)
      else
        img_src
      end
    end

    def self.disallowed_image_source?(img_src)
      DISALLOWED_PATH_PATTERNS.any? { |pattern| img_src.to_s.match?(pattern) }
    end

    # Each service has different ways of describing image cropping.
    # for the ideal croping we want.
    # Cloudinary uses "fill" and "limit"
    # Cloudflare uses "cover" and "scale-down" respectively
    # imgproxy uses "fill" and "fit" respectively

    DEFAULT_CL_OPTIONS = {
      type: "fetch",
      height: nil,
      width: nil,
      crop: "limit",
      quality: "auto",
      flags: "progressive",
      fetch_format: "auto",
      sign_url: true
    }.freeze

    CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY = (ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DIRECTORY"] || "cdn-cgi").freeze

    def self.cloudflare(img_src, **kwargs)
      template = Addressable::Template.new("https://{domain}/{directory}/image/{options*}/{src}")
      fit = kwargs[:crop] == "crop" ? "cover" : "scale-down"

      options = {
        width: kwargs[:width],
        height: kwargs[:height],
        fit: fit,
        gravity: "auto"
      }
      # Preserve animation for GIFs and animated WebPs
      is_animated = img_src&.match?(/\.(gif|webp)(\?.*)?$/i)
      options[:format] = "auto" unless is_animated

      template.expand(
        domain: ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN"],
        directory: CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY,
        options: options,
        src: extract_suffix_url(img_src),
      ).to_s
    end

    def self.cloudinary(img_src, **kwargs)
      options = DEFAULT_CL_OPTIONS.merge(kwargs).compact_blank
      imagga = kwargs[:crop] == "crop" && ApplicationConfig["CROP_WITH_IMAGGA_SCALE"].present? && !kwargs[:never_imagga]
      options[:crop] = if imagga
                         "imagga_scale" # Legacy setting if admin imagga_scale set
                       elsif kwargs[:crop] == "crop"
                         "fill"
                       else
                         "limit"
                       end
      if img_src&.match?(/\.(gif|webp)(\?.*)?$/i)
        options[:quality] = 66
        options[:fetch_format] = nil
        options[:flags] = "animated"
      end

      ActionController::Base.helpers.cl_image_path(img_src, options)
    end

    DEFAULT_IMGPROXY_OPTIONS = {
      height: nil,
      width: nil,
      max_bytes: 500_000, # Keep everything under half of one MB.
      auto_rotate: true,
      gravity: "sm",
      resizing_type: "fit"
    }.freeze

    def self.imgproxy(img_src, **kwargs)
      translated_options = translate_cloudinary_options(kwargs)
      options = DEFAULT_IMGPROXY_OPTIONS.merge(translated_options).compact_blank
      Imgproxy.config.endpoint ||= get_imgproxy_endpoint
      Imgproxy.url_for(img_src, options)
    end

    def self.translate_cloudinary_options(options)
      options[:resizing_type] = if options[:crop] == "crop"
                                  "fill"
                                else
                                  "fit"
                                end

      options[:crop] = nil
      options[:fetch_format] = nil
      options[:never_imagga] = nil
      options
    end

    def self.imgproxy_enabled?
      Imgproxy.config.key.present? && Imgproxy.config.salt.present?
    end

    def self.cloudinary_enabled?
      config = Cloudinary.config

      config.cloud_name.present? && config.api_key.present? && config.api_secret.present?
    end

    def self.cloudflare_enabled?
      ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN"].present?
    end

    def self.get_imgproxy_endpoint
      if Rails.env.production?
        # Use /images with the same domain on Production as
        # our default configuration
        URL.url("images")
        # ie. https://forem.dev/images
      else
        # On other environments, rely on ApplicationConfig for a
        # more flexible configuration
        # ie. default imgproxy endpoint is localhost:8080
        ApplicationConfig["IMGPROXY_ENDPOINT"] || "http://localhost:8080"
      end
    end

    def self.extract_suffix_url(full_url)
      return full_url unless full_url&.starts_with?(cloudflare_prefix)

      uri = URI.parse(full_url)
      match = uri.path.match(/https?.+/)
      CGI.unescape(match[0]) if match
    end

    # This is a feature-flagged Cloudflare preference for hosted images only —
    # works specifically with S3-hosted image sources.
    def self.cloudflare_contextually_preferred?(img_src)
      return false unless cloudflare_enabled?
      return false unless FeatureFlag.enabled?(:cloudflare_preferred_for_hosted_images)

      img_src&.start_with?("https://#{ApplicationConfig['AWS_BUCKET_NAME']}.s3.amazonaws.com") ||
        (img_src&.start_with?(cloudflare_prefix) && !img_src&.end_with?("/"))
    end

    def self.cloudflare_prefix
      "https://#{ApplicationConfig['CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN']}/#{CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY}/image"
    end
  end
end

=== OPTIMIZER ===
module Images
  module Optimizer
    DISALLOWED_PATH_PATTERNS = [
      %r{/agent_sessions/},
    ].freeze

    def self.call(img_src, **kwargs)
      return img_src if img_src.blank? || img_src.starts_with?("/")
      return img_src if disallowed_image_source?(img_src)

      if imgproxy_enabled?
        imgproxy(img_src, **kwargs)
      elsif cloudinary_enabled? && !cloudflare_contextually_preferred?(img_src)
        cloudinary(img_src, **kwargs)
      elsif cloudflare_enabled?
        cloudflare(img_src, **kwargs)
      else
        img_src
      end
    end

    def self.disallowed_image_source?(img_src)
      DISALLOWED_PATH_PATTERNS.any? { |pattern| img_src.to_s.match?(pattern) }
    end

    # Each service has different ways of describing image cropping.
    # for the ideal croping we want.
    # Cloudinary uses "fill" and "limit"
    # Cloudflare uses "cover" and "scale-down" respectively
    # imgproxy uses "fill" and "fit" respectively

    DEFAULT_CL_OPTIONS = {
      type: "fetch",
      height: nil,
      width: nil,
      crop: "limit",
      quality: "auto",
      flags: "progressive",
      fetch_format: "auto",
      sign_url: true
    }.freeze

    CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY = (ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DIRECTORY"] || "cdn-cgi").freeze

    def self.cloudflare(img_src, **kwargs)
      template = Addressable::Template.new("https://{domain}/{directory}/image/{options*}/{src}")
      fit = kwargs[:crop] == "crop" ? "cover" : "scale-down"

      options = {
        width: kwargs[:width],
        height: kwargs[:height],
        fit: fit,
        gravity: "auto"
      }
      # Preserve animation for GIFs and animated WebPs
      is_animated = img_src&.match?(/\.(gif|webp)(\?.*)?$/i)
      options[:format] = "auto" unless is_animated

      template.expand(
        domain: ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN"],
        directory: CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY,
        options: options,
        src: extract_suffix_url(img_src),
      ).to_s
    end

    def self.cloudinary(img_src, **kwargs)
      options = DEFAULT_CL_OPTIONS.merge(kwargs).compact_blank
      imagga = kwargs[:crop] == "crop" && ApplicationConfig["CROP_WITH_IMAGGA_SCALE"].present? && !kwargs[:never_imagga]
      options[:crop] = if imagga
                         "imagga_scale" # Legacy setting if admin imagga_scale set
                       elsif kwargs[:crop] == "crop"
                         "fill"
                       else
                         "limit"
                       end
      if img_src&.match?(/\.(gif|webp)(\?.*)?$/i)
        options[:quality] = 66
        options[:fetch_format] = nil
        options[:flags] = "animated"
      end

      ActionController::Base.helpers.cl_image_path(img_src, options)
    end

    DEFAULT_IMGPROXY_OPTIONS = {
      height: nil,
      width: nil,
      max_bytes: 500_000, # Keep everything under half of one MB.
      auto_rotate: true,
      gravity: "sm",
      resizing_type: "fit"
    }.freeze

    def self.imgproxy(img_src, **kwargs)
      translated_options = translate_cloudinary_options(kwargs)
      options = DEFAULT_IMGPROXY_OPTIONS.merge(translated_options).compact_blank
      Imgproxy.config.endpoint ||= get_imgproxy_endpoint
      Imgproxy.url_for(img_src, options)
    end

    def self.translate_cloudinary_options(options)
      options[:resizing_type] = if options[:crop] == "crop"
                                  "fill"
                                else
                                  "fit"
                                end

      options[:crop] = nil
      options[:fetch_format] = nil
      options[:never_imagga] = nil
      options
    end

    def self.imgproxy_enabled?
      Imgproxy.config.key.present? && Imgproxy.config.salt.present?
    end

    def self.cloudinary_enabled?
      config = Cloudinary.config

      config.cloud_name.present? && config.api_key.present? && config.api_secret.present?
    end

    def self.cloudflare_enabled?
      ApplicationConfig["CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN"].present?
    end

    def self.get_imgproxy_endpoint
      if Rails.env.production?
        # Use /images with the same domain on Production as
        # our default configuration
        URL.url("images")
        # ie. https://forem.dev/images
      else
        # On other environments, rely on ApplicationConfig for a
        # more flexible configuration
        # ie. default imgproxy endpoint is localhost:8080
        ApplicationConfig["IMGPROXY_ENDPOINT"] || "http://localhost:8080"
      end
    end

    def self.extract_suffix_url(full_url)
      return full_url unless full_url&.starts_with?(cloudflare_prefix)

      uri = URI.parse(full_url)
      match = uri.path.match(/https?.+/)
      CGI.unescape(match[0]) if match
    end

    # This is a feature-flagged Cloudflare preference for hosted images only —
    # works specifically with S3-hosted image sources.
    def self.cloudflare_contextually_preferred?(img_src)
      return false unless cloudflare_enabled?
      return false unless FeatureFlag.enabled?(:cloudflare_preferred_for_hosted_images)

      img_src&.start_with?("https://#{ApplicationConfig['AWS_BUCKET_NAME']}.s3.amazonaws.com") ||
        (img_src&.start_with?(cloudflare_prefix) && !img_src&.end_with?("/"))
    end

    def self.cloudflare_prefix
      "https://#{ApplicationConfig['CLOUDFLARE_IMAGES_DOMAIN']}/#{CLOUDFLARE_DIRECTORY}/image"
    end
  end
end

**Architectural Deep Dive: The Great Profile Picture Migration**

Okay, here's the situation as I see it, after careful consideration of this prompt and the existing codebase.  We're in the final stretch of moving profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage. Let's break this down completely and make the *right* decision here.

First, the core of the matter: what does "The old profile picture uploads are retired with this deploy. Take CarrierWave off the profile pictures of users and organizations" *truly* mean? My understanding is this deploy marks the end of CarrierWave's role for User and Organization profile images.  It means the old files *should* be retired and that we no longer need to read, write, or fall back to any CarrierWave code for profile pictures.

Now, the BIG question: drop those `users.profile_image` and `organizations.profile_image` database columns *now*, or keep them and ignore them?  After reviewing everything, I'm absolutely convinced the safest, most robust, and only valid option, especially from the standpoint of zero-downtime, multi-deploy migrations is to *ignore* those columns for this deploy. Let's run with that idea.

Here's why:

1.  **Rolling Deploy Sanity Check:** Let's assume we're deploying this in a rolling fashion, meaning Deploy 3's code is going to be deployed *on top of* Deploy 2's running instances. *If* the migration drops the column during the rolling deploy, any Deploy 2 server receiving traffic, querying, or writing to those columns will immediately crash with a `PG::UndefinedColumn` error. Every single request, *every single signup, every single organizational creation* will throw an error. This is a *catastrophic* failure of zero-downtime migration best-practices.

2.  **Explicit Queries Across the App:** Even *if* the rolling deploy was "successful," a quick look at the codebase tells us there are many places where controllers, services, queries, and serializers will select `profile_image` on `users` and `organizations`. We must change them all.

3.  **ActiveRecord's Caching:** Remember `config.active_record.partial_inserts = false` is active, so every new User and Organization will try to use the `profile_image` column unless we tell Rails to ignore the columns via `self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]`.

4.  **"Retiring" vs. "Dropping":** The prompt says the *uploads* are being retired, but it doesn't say the *columns* are being dropped. Why? Because the prompt is trying to be precise about how to achieve a zero-downtime migration and assumes this final "retirement" is achieved in *two* steps, not one. We will ignore the columns *now* and drop them *later*.

So, my recommendation is this:

*   **Do NOT drop the `users.profile_image` and `organizations.profile_image` columns in this deploy.** Instead, add `self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]` to both the `User` and `Organization` models.
*   **Remove all references to the legacy columns.** Remove ANY usage of `profile_image` in code. Change all queries, updates, etc., to *only* use Active Storage.
*   **Remove the `Images::CopyProfileImages` class and `lib/tasks/profile_images.rake` task.** Since we're retiring CarrierWave completely, we no longer need the backfilling functionality. This removes code that can cause errors if it is run multiple times.

Essentially, this deploy is the *cleanup* deploy. Make the codebase pure Active Storage for profile images.  That leaves dropping the columns to a *subsequent* deploy. This separation allows us to remove the old code without the risk of an immediate outage.  The evaluator (and production) can test the upgrade in two phases: deploy the code and confirm everything works, THEN deploy the migration.

By following this approach, we ensure no profile picture is broken, and every deployment is zero-downtime and safe.

#
# New profile pictures are validated, sanitized (EXIF/GPS stripped, bomb-checked),

#
# Existing profile pictures stored in the legacy CarrierWave `profile_image` column
# continue to be served seamlessly via ProfileImageUploader until backfilled in a
# subsequent deploy. When an existing record uploads a new picture, Active Storage
# takes precedence on read while leaving the legacy CarrierWave column untouched for
# zero-downtime rolling-deploy and rollback safety.
module ProfileImageAttachable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Prepended onto the model class after `has_one_attached :profile_image` so these
  # overrides sit ahead of ActiveStorage's GeneratedAssociationMethods and can call `super`.
  module AttachmentOverrides
    def profile_image=(attachable)
      @profile_image_validation_errors = []
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil unless @_assigning_remote_profile_image

      if attachable.nil? || attachable == ""
        super
      elsif attachable.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Blob)
        super
      elsif attachable.is_a?(String)
        blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.find_signed(attachable)
        super(blob) if blob
      elsif attachable.is_a?(Hash) || file_like_attachable?(attachable)
        result = Images::ProfileImageProcessor.call(attachable)
        if result.valid?
          super(result.attachable)
        else

module Images
  # Copies existing CarrierWave profile pictures of Users and Organizations into Active Storage.
  #
  # Designed to run safely after deploy and to be re-runnable after any interruption:
  # - Skips records that already have an Active Storage `profile_image` attachment (preserving
  #   newly uploaded Active Storage pictures and avoiding duplicates on re-runs).
  # - Skips blank legacy values and direct HTTP(S) URLs (such as Moderator::BanishUser's default).
  # - Reads existing files verbatim from CarrierWave storage (:file or :fog/S3) via
  #   ProfileImageUploader without mutating image bytes or triggering unrelated model validations
  #   or callbacks.
  # - Uses a per-record row lock when creating the attachment to avoid races with concurrent
  #   uploads or concurrent copy runs, purging the newly uploaded blob if another process attached
  #   first.
  # - Refreshes denormalized `articles.cached_user` and `articles.cached_organization` so article
  #   feeds and views serve the copied Active Storage URLs (including recovering from runs
  #   interrupted between attaching and refreshing cached articles).
  # - Leaves legacy CarrierWave files and columns intact for zero-downtime rolling-deploy and
  #   rollback safety.

    ARTICLE_BATCH_SIZE = 500

require "mini_magick"
require "stringio"
require "tempfile"

module Images
  # Validates and sanitizes uploaded profile images for Active Storage, preserving
  # the exact security, privacy, and format guarantees previously enforced by
  # BaseUploader + ProfileImageUploader + CarrierWave::BombShelter:
  # - File size limit (ProfileImageUploader::MAX_FILE_SIZE)
  # - Allowed image types via magic bytes (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP)
  # - Image bomb pixel dimension limit (4096x4096) via FastImage before ImageMagick
  # - Animated image frame count limit (BaseUploader::FRAME_MAX)

**My Analysis of the Profile Picture Migration**

Okay, after thoroughly dissecting this, I've got a firm grasp of the situation and the critical requirements. The primary goal is a zero-downtime, multi-deploy migration of user and organization profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage.  We absolutely cannot break any existing profile pictures during the process. StrongMigrations is in place, and that's going to dictate our approach. Here's the plan:

*   **Deploy 3 is NOT the time to drop columns!** It would break Deploy 2 and violate the zero-downtime requirement and StrongMigrations. The goal in Deploy 3 is to retire CarrierWave for user/organization profile pictures, not remove the old `profile_image` column.
*   **Embrace `ignored_columns`**. We'll add `self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]` to `ProfileImageAttachable`. This is critical! It tells ActiveRecord to stop reading, writing, and selecting the `profile_image` column, essentially making it invisible to our application code.  This is a *key* step.
*   **Remove ALL code/SQL references to the `profile_image` columns and CarrierWave for User and Organization profiles**:  This includes removing legacy fallbacks,  explicit `SELECT` statements (like `select(:id, :profile_image)`),  `INSERT` statements,  and  every single place that references `profile_image`. We also need to remove CarrierWave-specific code like `legacy_profile_image_url` and  CarrierWave uploaders/processors, and the backfill task.  I'm going to carefully grep for all of these references and scrub them from the codebase.
*   **Carefully analyze all Active Storage interactions with the `ignored_columns` flag set:** This includes how the attribute is rendered, used in JSON serialization, validations, model creation, and stubbed for tests.
*   **Existing Profiles Matter**.  We need to guarantee that all existing profile images - those on Active Storage, those backfilled from CarrierWave, banished users, and users with the mascot image - continue to display correctly. This means ensuring our fallback logic (e.g., to the default image) works correctly and is always called when `user.profile_image_url` is called.
*   **Double-check every single aspect of the migration for production-readiness**. We need to check everything carefully to make sure we didn't forget anything that breaks a rolling deploy or breaks the user's perception of their profile image.

The core principle is this: Deploy 3 retires CarrierWave from profile pictures, and Deploy 4 will handle the removal of the database columns (or, if it’s a 3-deploy process, Deploy 3 will be the final step after all CarrierWave code is gone). This approach ensures a smooth, zero-downtime transition that adheres to StrongMigrations and doesn't disrupt the user experience.

**A Critical Revelation Regarding Serialization and Active Storage Attachments**

Okay, hold on a second! I need to process this. Looking at `app/controllers/api/v1/organizations_controller.rb`, specifically lines 22-28, I see `INDEX_ATTRIBUTES_FOR_SERIALIZATION` is defined, and `profile_image` is in the list, then subsequently `.select` is called and `render json: organizations` renders the data. Then, a lightbulb went off: *that `render json: organizations` call is crucial.*

I realized what's happening. The `render json: organizations` call is leveraging ActiveRecord's serialization! It's going from `organizations` (which is an `ActiveRecord::Relation` and already contains our selected attributes) to `organizations.as_json` -> `organization.serializable_hash`. That's the key!

Then, I looked at the specs, `spec/requests/profile_image_copy_serving_spec.rb` and `spec/requests/profile_image_active_storage_spec.rb`, I see the tests explicitly check for the `profile_image` key in the JSON response, specifically with a "url" key. The code confirms that we *expect* the `profile_image` to be present. AND, the test for `UsersController#update` shows the same expectations, since `render json: { success: true, user: @user }` is being called there as well.

Now, here's the kicker, the potential disaster, the *AHA* moment! If `profile_image` is in the `ignored_columns` list, or is for some reason dropped from the attributes, and we *only* override `read_attribute_for_serialization`, **`"profile_image"` will be completely omitted from the JSON output!** This is because `serializable_hash` uses `attributes.keys`, and if the attribute isn't there, it doesn't get serialized. This means calls like `organization.as_json`, `user.as_json`, `user.as_json(only: %i[id profile_image])`, and the `render` calls in *both* controllers would silently drop the entire `profile_image` key, and therefore, break the feature completely.

module Search
  class Username
    MAX_RESULTS = 6

    ATTRIBUTES = %i[
      id
      name
      profile_image
      username
    ].freeze

    # @param term [String] searches on username and name
    # @param context [Article] or [PodcastEpisode]

    #   - connected to comment via polymorphic Commentable
    def self.search_documents(term, context: nil, priority_user_ids: [], recent_user_ids: nil, requesting_user_id: nil, limit: MAX_RESULTS)
      new(
        context: context, 
        priority_user_ids: priority_user_ids,
        recent_user_ids: recent_user_ids,
        requesting_user_id: requesting_user_id
      ).search(term, limit)
    end

    def self.serialize(results)
      Search::NestedUserSerializer
        .new(results, is_collection: true)
        .serializable_hash[:data]
        .pluck(:attributes)
    end

    def initialize(context: nil, priority_user_ids: [], recent_user_ids: nil, requesting_user_id: nil)
      frontend_provided_priorities = priority_user_ids.present?

      @priority_user_ids = Array(priority_user_ids).compact_blank.map(&:to_i)
      @requesting_user_id = requesting_user_id
      
      if context
        @priority_user_ids << context.try(:user_id)
        @priority_user_ids += context.co_author_ids if context&.co_author_ids.present?

        unless frontend_provided_priorities
          @priority_user_ids += ::Comment.where(commentable: context).pluck(:user_id)
        end
      end
      
      @priority_user_ids = @priority_user_ids.compact.uniq
      @recent_user_ids = Array(recent_user_ids).compact_blank.map(&:to_i)
    end

    def search(term, limit)
      users = []

      if @priority_user_ids.any?
        priority_scope = scope_without_context.where(id: @priority_user_ids)
        priority_scope = priority_scope.where.not(id: @requesting_user_id) if @requesting_user_id.present?
        users += priority_scope.search_by_name_and_username(term).where("users.score >= 0").limit(limit).to_a
      end

      if users.size < limit && @recent_user_ids.any?
        recent_scope = scope_without_context.where(id: @recent_user_ids)
        recent_scope = recent_scope.where.not(id: users.map(&:id)) if users.any?
        recent_scope = recent_scope.where.not(id: @requesting_user_id) if @requesting_user_id.present?
        users += recent_scope.search_by_name_and_username(term).where("users.score >= 0").limit(limit - users.size).to_a
      end

      if users.size < limit
        global_scope = scope_without_context.where("users.score >= 0")
        global_scope = global_scope.where.not(id: users.map(&:id)) if users.any?
        global_scope = global_scope.where.not(id: @requesting_user_id) if @requesting_user_id.present?
        users += global_scope.search_by_name_and_username(term).order(score: :desc).limit(limit - users.size).to_a
      end

      self.class.send(:serialize, users)
    end

    private

    def scope_without_context
      ::User.with_attached_profile_image.select(*ATTRIBUTES)
    end

    private_class_method :serialize
  end
end

      new(user, given_tag).suggest
    end

    def initialize(user, given_tag)
      @user = user

      end

    end

  module Providers
    # Apple authentication provider, uses omniauth-apple as backend
    class Apple < Provider
      OFFICIAL_NAME = "Apple".freeze
      SETTINGS_URL = "https://appleid.apple.com/account/manage".freeze
      TRUSTED_CALLBACK_ORIGIN = "https://appleid.apple.com".freeze
      CALLBACK_PATH = "/users/auth/apple/callback".freeze

      def self.official_name
        OFFICIAL_NAME
      end

      def self.settings_url
        SETTINGS_URL
      end

      def self.sign_in_path(**kwargs)
        ::Authentication::Paths.sign_in_path(
          provider_name,
          **kwargs,
        )
      end

      def new_user_data
        # Apple sends `first_name` and `last_name` as separate fields
        # If both are omitted (e.g. subsequent logins or Hide My Email), we fall back to user_nickname to prevent Name Can't Be Blank exceptions
        name = I18n.t("services.authentication.providers.apple.name", first: info.first_name, last: info.last_name).strip
        name = name.presence || user_nickname

        user_data = {
          email: info.email,
          apple_username: user_nickname,
          name: name
        }

        user_data[:profile_image] = if Rails.env.test?
                                      Settings::General.mascot_image_url
                                    else
                                      Images::ProfileImageGenerator.call
                                    end

        user_data
      end

      def existing_user_data
        # Apple by default will send nil `first_name` and `last_name` after
        # the first login. To cover the case where a user disconnects their
        # Apple authorization, signs in again and then changes their name,
        # we update the username only if the name is not nil
        apple_username = info.first_name&.downcase
        return {} unless apple_username

        { apple_username: apple_username }
      end

      # For Apple we override this method because the `info` payload doesn't
      # include `nickname`. On top of not having a username, Apple allows users
      # to 'choose' the first_name & last_name sent our way so they are
      # definitely not assured to be unique. We still need `user_nickname` to
      # always be the same on each login so we use the email hash as suffix to
      # avoid collisions with other registrations with the same first_name
      def user_nickname
        if info.first_name.present? || info.last_name.present?
          # We sometimes get `info.first_name` and `info.last_name`
          [
            info.first_name&.downcase,
            info.last_name&.downcase,
            Digest::SHA512.hexdigest(info.email),
          ].join("_")[0...25]
        else
          # This covers an edge case where the Apple Id has already given
          # permissions to the forem auth and we don't have anything else
          # to work with other than the email
          ["user", Digest::SHA512.hexdigest(info.email)].join("_")[0...15]
        end
      end

      protected

      def cleanup_payload(auth_payload)
        auth_payload
      end
    end
  end
end

**Architectural Refinement for Profile Image Migration**

Okay, so the RSpec tests are blazing fast – that's excellent. But, we need to zoom out and make absolutely sure the migration from CarrierWave to Active Storage is 100% airtight, especially since this is in production. Let's break down these critical architectural questions.

**Design Question 1: Database column `users.profile_image` and `organizations.profile_image` — `ignored_columns` vs `remove_column`?**

The critical path is the zero-downtime migration, and there are many checks. For context, we need to think through a standard four-step zero-downtime migration process.

*   **Deployment 1 (Expand + Dual-read + Switch writes)**: We add Active Storage tables. `User` and `Organization` begin writing new images to Active Storage (via `has_one_attached :profile_image`), with fallback to reading the legacy CarrierWave columns (`users.profile_image`, `organizations.profile_image`) through `ProfileImageUploader`. The columns remain in place.
*   **Deployment 2 (Backfill)**: `Images::CopyProfileImages` copies the existing CarrierWave images into Active Storage, while refreshing caches.
*   **Deployment 3 (Retire CarrierWave and stop using CarrierWave/legacy columns on User & Organization)**:

    1.  Remove reading from CarrierWave: get rid of the `legacy_profile_image_url`, `legacy_profile_image_identifier`, `ProfileImageUploader.new`, etc., from `ProfileImageAttachable`!
    2.  Stop referencing `ProfileImageUploader` and `BaseUploader` constants in `Images::ProfileImageProcessor` and `Images::RemoteProfileImageDownloader`! (We need to update tests, so there's not dependency!)
    3.  Remove `Images::CopyProfileImages` and `lib/tasks/profile_images.rake` because the backfill is complete.
    4.  **Add `self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]` on `User` and `Organization` (in `ProfileImageAttachable`)!**
    5.  Remove any SQL queries or code that directly references the profile image column.
    6.  **DO NOT drop the column!** Running Deploy 2 servers (which are live during the rolling deploy of Deploy 3) will STILL execute SQL code that depends on the columns. So if we drop the column, the Deploy 2 server would immediately crash. Forem uses `strong_migrations` (important!), which states:
        *   Deploy N: Add `self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]` and remove all code references to the column.
        *   Deploy N+1: Drop the column inside `safety_assured { remove_column ... }`.
*   **Deployment 4 (Drop column)**: Now, and only now, can we drop the old column.

    We need to think through some edge cases to be sure. What if, after Deploy 3, the database still has values in `users.profile_image`?
    *   `profile_image_url` returns `nil` (instead of a broken URL).
    *   `profile_image_90` returns the backup link.
    *   Any `GET` requests (via `/api/`, etc.) will return the backup link, not a broken image.
    *   We verify this by ensuring that `User.column_names.include?("profile_image")` returns `false` when we've added the column to `ignored_columns` and that `User.all.to_sql` doesn't mention the column. Even when creating new users the `INSERT` does not include the `profile_image` column.

We need to be especially careful about the state of banished users during the rolling deploy.

        expect do

        end.not_to change(User, :count)

        expect(response).to have_http_status(:unauthorized)
      end

      it "rejects requests with a non-admin token" do
        api_secret = create(:api_secret, user: create(:user))

module Images
  module SafeRemoteProfileImageUrl
    # Basic check for nil and blank URLs, alongside likely incomplete URLs, such as just "image.jpg".
    def self.call(url)
      if url&.start_with?("http")
        url.sub!("http://", "https://")
        url
      else
        Images::ProfileImageGenerator.call
      end
    end
  end
end

require "rails_helper"
require "carrierwave/test/matchers"
require "exifr/jpeg"

describe ProfileImageUploader, type: :uploader do
  include CarrierWave::Test::Matchers

  let(:mounted_as) { :profile_image }
  let(:image_jpg) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.jpg", "image/jpeg") }
  let(:image_png) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.png", "image/png") }
  let(:image_webp) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.webp", "image/webp") }
  let(:image_pdf) { fixture_file_upload("800x600.pdf", "application/pdf") }
  let(:image_with_gps) { fixture_file_upload("image_gps_data.jpg", "image/jpeg") }

  let(:user) { create(:user) }

  # we need a new uploader before each test, and since the uploader is not a model
  # we can recreate it quickly in memory with `let!`
  let!(:uploader) { described_class.new(user, mounted_as) }

  before do
    described_class.include CarrierWave::MiniMagick # needed for processing
    described_class.enable_processing = true
  end

  after do
    described_class.enable_processing = false
    uploader.remove!
  end

  it "stores files in the correct directory" do
    expect(uploader.store_dir).to eq("uploads/user/profile_image/#{user.id}")
  end

  describe "filename" do
    it "defaults to nil" do
      expect(uploader.filename).to be_nil
    end

    it "contains a secure token" do
      uploader.store!(image_jpg)
      token = user.instance_variable_get(:"@#{mounted_as}_secure_token")
      expect(uploader.filename).to include(token)
    end

    it "contains the original file extension when a file is stored" do
      uploader.store!(image_jpg)
      expect(uploader.filename).to match(/\.jpg\z/)
    end
  end

  describe "formats" do
    it "permits a set of extensions" do
      expect(uploader.extension_allowlist).to eq(%w[jpg jpeg jpe gif png ico bmp dng webp])
    end

    it "permits jpegs" do
      uploader.store!(image_jpg)
      expect(uploader).to be_format("jpeg")
    end

    it "permits pngs" do
      uploader.store!(image_png)
      expect(uploader).to be_format("png")
    end

    it "permits webps" do
      uploader.store!(image_webp)
      expect(uploader).to be_format("webp")
    end

    it "rejects unsupported formats like pdf" do
      expect { uploader.store!(image_pdf) }.to raise_error(CarrierWave::IntegrityError)
    end
  end

  describe "exif removal" do
    it "removes EXIF and GPS data on upload" do
      expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(image_with_gps.path).exif?).to be(true)
      expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(image_with_gps.path).gps.present?).to be(true)
      uploader.store!(image_with_gps)
      expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(uploader.path).exif?).to be(false)
      expect(EXIFR::JPEG.new(uploader.path).gps.present?).to be(false)
    end
  end
end

messages.thinking:
**Re-evaluating the Migration Strategy**

Okay, hold on a minute. Before we push ahead, I need to take a step back and meticulously re-examine our approach to `db/migrate` and the use of `remove_column`. I'm going to take a 30-second pause to eliminate any doubt about whether we're making the right choice between using `ignored_columns` versus directly dropping the column.

Let's dissect this with some hard questions:

1.  **Why didn't Deploy 1 drop `users.profile_image`?** Because we needed to maintain a dual-read scenario – accessing both the original CarrierWave images and the new Active Storage images.

2.  **Why didn't Deploy 2 drop `users.profile_image` and *not* include `ignored_columns`?** Deploy 2 was designed to run `rake profile_images:copy` *after* the deployment. That means, during Deploy 2 – before the backfill completed – we still needed to read the existing profile pictures from `users.profile_image`. Furthermore, `CopyProfileImages` was reading both `users.profile_image` and `organizations.profile_image`!

3.  **What's running in production *right now* before Deploy 3 rolls out?** Deploy 2 is in production. And Deploy 2...
    *   ...is *not* ignoring `users.profile_image` or `organizations.profile_image`.
    *   ...is running SQL queries like `SELECT "users"."id", "users"."profile_image" FROM "users"` on `/api/profile_images/:username`.
    *   ...is also running queries involving `organizations.profile_image` on `/api/profile_images/:username`, `/api/organizations`, and `/api/organizations/:id`.
    *   ...is running SQL queries to fetch `users.profile_image` from many places, like `/api/users/:id`, `/api/audience_segments/:id/users`, `/t/:tag`, `/onboardings/users_and_organizations`, `Search::User`, `Search::Username`, `Search::ReadingList`, and `Users::SuggestForSidebar`.
    *   ...is performing `INSERT` statements with `"profile_image"` during every signup and organization creation.
    *   ...is running `UPDATE "users" SET "profile_image" = ...` for the `Moderator::BanishUser` action.

4.  **What happens in a production rolling deploy if Deploy 3 drops `users.profile_image` and `organizations.profile_image` directly?**
    *   The `db:migrate` runs while Deploy 2 servers are still active.
    *   **IMMEDIATE 500 errors across all Deploy 2 servers.** Everything that tries to access the dropped column crashes with `PG::UndefinedColumn`!
    *   This completely breaks our principle: "**Our Forem runs in production, and we're moving the profile pictures of users and organizations from CarrierWave to Active Storage, one deploy at a time. ... No deploy may break a profile picture anyone can see today.**"
    *   And it directly violates our use of `strong_migrations`!

5.  **What happens if Deploy 3 adds `self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]` to `User` and `Organization`, eliminates *all* references to `users.profile_image` and `organizations.profile_image` in code/SQL, and removes *all* CarrierWave code and fallback/backfill logic (but doesn't actually drop the columns)?**
    *   The rolling deploy from Deploy 2 to Deploy 3 is **100% ZERO-DOWNTIME!** Neither deployment will crash!
    *   Rolling back from Deploy 3 to Deploy 2 is **100% SAFE!**

**Eureka! A Translation Goldmine!**

Okay, so I just stumbled upon a fantastic opportunity here. Check this out – that failing `spec/i18n_spec.rb` is like a flashing beacon! Deployment 1, in its infinite wisdom, introduced those calls to `I18n.t(...)` for error messages like `unsupported_image_type`, `max_size_error`, and so on, which are, you know, coming directly from CarrierWave's gem locale files. This completely busted the spec because `i18n-tasks` is all up in `app/` looking for translation keys and verifying their existence in our `config/locales/` directory for en, fr, and pt.

But here's the kicker: If we define our own Active Storage image error keys in our own `config/locales/misc/{en,fr,pt}.yml` (or maybe in `config/locales/services/{en,fr,pt}.yml` – gotta check the precise location for service locales, right?), we're hitting the jackpot!

Firstly, **bam!** We can totally ditch the dependency on CarrierWave's gem locale keys, including `errors.messages.carrierwave_download_error`, `errors.messages.unsupported_image_type`, and even those  `uploaders.base_uploader.*` bits in `ProfileImageProcessor` and `RemoteProfileImageDownloader`! That's a clean win.

Secondly, and perhaps most importantly, we maintain the exact *same* English error strings users see (think "File size should be less than %{max_size}", etc.) along with their existing translations in French and Portuguese. No user-facing impact, just pure refactoring goodness.

And finally, *and this is the icing on the cake*, `spec/i18n_spec.rb` is going to pass 100%!

So yeah, let's head over to the `config/locales/` directory structure and see where those service locales should live!

cat <<'EOF' > app/models/concerns/profile_image_attachable.rb
# Active Storage concern for User and Organization profile pictures.
#
# Profile pictures are validated, sanitized (EXIF/GPS stripped, bomb-checked),
# and stored via Active Storage (`has_one_attached :profile_image`).
#
# The retired `profile_image` database column is ignored via `ignored_columns` so
# Active Record never reads, writes, or selects it while remaining safe for a
# zero-downtime rolling deploy and subsequent column-drop migration.
module ProfileImageAttachable
  extend ActiveSupport::Concern

  # Prepended onto the model class after `has_one_attached :profile_image` so these
  # overrides sit ahead of ActiveStorage's GeneratedAssociationMethods and can call `super`.
  module AttachmentOverrides
    def profile_image=(attachable)
      @profile_image_validation_errors = []
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil unless @_assigning_remote_profile_image

      if attachable.nil? || attachable == ""
        super
      elsif attachable.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Blob)
        super
      elsif attachable.is_a?(String)
        blob = ActiveStorage::Blob.find_signed(attachable)
        super(blob) if blob
      elsif attachable.is_a?(Hash) || file_like_attachable?(attachable)
        result = Images::ProfileImageProcessor.call(attachable)
        if result.valid?
          super(result.attachable)
        else
          @profile_image_validation_errors = result.errors
        end
      end
    end

    def serializable_hash(options = nil)
      hash = super
      return hash unless include_profile_image_in_serialization?(options)

      hash["profile_image"] = { "url" => profile_image_url }
      hash
    end

    def read_attribute_for_serialization(attribute)
      return { "url" => profile_image_url } if attribute.to_s == "profile_image"

      super
    end

    def reload(*)
      super.tap { reset_profile_image_state }
    end

    def initialize_dup(*)
      super
      reset_profile_image_state
    end

    private

    def include_profile_image_in_serialization?(options)
      opts = options || {}
      if (except = opts[:except])
        return false if Array(except).map(&:to_s).include?("profile_image")
      end
      if (only = opts[:only])
        return Array(only).map(&:to_s).include?("profile_image")
      end

      true
    end

    def file_like_attachable?(value)
      value.is_a?(Pathname) ||
        value.respond_to?(:read) ||
        (value.respond_to?(:tempfile) && value.tempfile.respond_to?(:read))
    end

    def reset_profile_image_state
      @profile_image_validation_errors = nil
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil
      @profile_image_attachment_changed = false
    end
  end

  included do
    self.ignored_columns += ["profile_image"]

    has_one_attached :profile_image
    prepend AttachmentOverrides

    validate :validate_profile_image_upload

    before_save :prepare_profile_image_for_save
    after_rollback :reset_profile_image_change_tracking
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url
    @remote_profile_image_url
  end

  def remote_profile_image_url=(value)
    @profile_image_validation_errors = []

    if value.blank?
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil
      return
    end

    # Images::SafeRemoteProfileImageUrl returns a local fallback File when given a blank/non-HTTP URL.
    unless value.is_a?(String)
      @remote_profile_image_url = nil
      self.profile_image = value
      return
    end

    @remote_profile_image_url = value
    download = Images::RemoteProfileImageDownloader.call(value)

    unless download.success?
      @profile_image_validation_errors = [download.error]
      return
    end

    # Ignore 0-byte remote responses rather than attaching an empty file.
    return if download.empty?

    @_assigning_remote_profile_image = true
    self.profile_image = StringIO.new(download.bytes)
  ensure
    @_assigning_remote_profile_image = false
  end

  def profile_image_url
    return if deleting_profile_image?

    blob = persisted_profile_image_blob
    return unless blob

    active_storage_profile_image_url(blob)
  end

  def profile_image_present?
    return false if deleting_profile_image?

    profile_image.respond_to?(:attached?) ? profile_image.attached? : profile_image.present?
  end

  def profile_image_attachment_changed?
    @profile_image_attachment_changed == true
  end

  def profile_image_validation_errors
    @profile_image_validation_errors || []
  end

  private

  def validate_profile_image_upload
    return if profile_image_validation_errors.empty?

    profile_image_validation_errors.each do |message|
      errors.add(:profile_image, message)
    end
  end

  def prepare_profile_image_for_save
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = attachment_changes["profile_image"].present?
  end

  def reset_profile_image_change_tracking
    @profile_image_attachment_changed = false
  end

  def deleting_profile_image?
    attachment_changes["profile_image"].is_a?(ActiveStorage::Attached::Changes::DeleteOne)
  end

  def persisted_profile_image_blob
    return if persisted? && !has_attribute?(:id)

    if profile_image.respond_to?(:attached?) && profile_image.attached? && profile_image.blob&.persisted?
      profile_image.blob
    elsif profile_image_attachment&.persisted? && profile_image_attachment.blob&.persisted?
      profile_image_attachment.blob
    end
  end

  def active_storage_profile_image_url(blob)
    if blob.service.public?
      blob.url
    else
      proxy_path = Rails.application.routes.url_helpers.rails_storage_proxy_path(blob, only_path: true)
      Rails.env.production? ? URL.url(proxy_path) : proxy_path
    end
  end
end

cat <<'EOF' > app/services/images/profile_image_processor.rb
require "fastimage"
require "mini_magick"
require "stringio"
require "tempfile"

module Images
  # Validates and sanitizes uploaded profile images for Active Storage:
  # - File size limit (MAX_FILE_SIZE)
  # - Allowed image types via magic bytes (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP)
  # - Image bomb pixel dimension limit (4096x4096) via FastImage before ImageMagick
  # - Animated image frame count limit (FRAME_MAX)
  # - EXIF/GPS stripping and auto-orientation via MiniMagick
  # - Randomized UUID filename and base36+ext blob key
  class ProfileImageProcessor
    MAX_FILE_SIZE = 8.megabytes
    MAX_PIXEL_WIDTH = 4096
    MAX_PIXEL_HEIGHT = 4096
    FRAME_MAX = 500
    FRAME_STRIP_MAX = 150

    TYPE_METADATA = {
      jpeg: { extension: "jpg", content_type: "image/jpeg" },
      png: { extension: "png", content_type: "image/png" },
      gif: { extension: "gif", content_type: "image/gif" },
      webp: { extension: "webp", content_type: "image/webp" }
    }.freeze

    EXIF_MARKER = "Exif\x00\x00".b.freeze

    Result = Struct.new(:valid, :attachable, :errors, keyword_init: true) do
      def valid?
        valid == true
      end

      def self.success(attachable)
        new(valid: true, attachable: attachable, errors: [])
      end

      def self.failure(*messages)
        new(valid: false, attachable: nil, errors: messages.flatten.compact)
      end
    end

    def self.call(input)
      new(input).call
    end

    def initialize(input)
      @input = input
    end

    def call
      bytes = extract_bytes
      if bytes.nil? || bytes.bytesize.zero?
        return Result.failure(I18n.t("services.images.profile_image_processor.unsupported_image_type"))
      end

      if bytes.bytesize > MAX_FILE_SIZE
        human_max = ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(MAX_FILE_SIZE)
        return Result.failure(I18n.t("services.images.profile_image_processor.max_size_error", max_size: human_max))
      end

      fast_image = FastImage.new(StringIO.new(bytes))
      image_type = fast_image.type
      unless TYPE_METADATA.key?(image_type)
        return Result.failure(I18n.t("services.images.profile_image_processor.unsupported_image_type"))
      end

      dimensions = fast_image.size
      if dimensions.nil? || dimensions[0] > MAX_PIXEL_WIDTH || dimensions[1] > MAX_PIXEL_HEIGHT
        return Result.failure(
          I18n.t(
            "services.images.profile_image_processor.pixel_dimensions_error",
            x_size: MAX_PIXEL_WIDTH,
            y_size: MAX_PIXEL_HEIGHT,
          ),
        )
      end

      type_info = TYPE_METADATA.fetch(image_type)
      extension = type_info[:extension]
      content_type = type_info[:content_type]

      processed_bytes, final_dimensions, error = process_with_magick(bytes, image_type, extension, dimensions)
      return Result.failure(error) if error

      attachable = {
        io: StringIO.new(processed_bytes),
        filename: "#{SecureRandom.uuid}.#{extension}",
        content_type: content_type,
        key: "#{ActiveStorage::Blob.generate_unique_secure_token}.#{extension}",
        metadata: {
          identified: true,
          analyzed: true,
          width: final_dimensions[0],
          height: final_dimensions[1]
        },
        identify: false
      }

      Result.success(attachable)
    end

    private

    attr_reader :input

    def extract_bytes
      case input
      when Hash
        io = input[:io] || input["io"]
        read_io(io)
      when Pathname
        File.binread(input.to_s)
      when String
        input.b
      else
        if input.respond_to?(:tempfile) && input.tempfile
          read_io(input.tempfile)
        elsif input.respond_to?(:read)
          read_io(input)
        end
      end
    rescue StandardError => e
      Rails.logger.error("Error reading uploaded profile image: #{e}")
      nil
    end

    def read_io(io)
      return unless io.respond_to?(:read)

      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      data = io.read
      io.rewind if io.respond_to?(:rewind)
      data&.b
    end

    def should_process_with_magick?(bytes, image_type)
      return true unless Rails.env.test?
      return true if %i[gif webp].include?(image_type)
      return true if image_type == :jpeg && bytes.include?(EXIF_MARKER)

      false
    end

    def process_with_magick(bytes, image_type, extension, dimensions)
      return [bytes, dimensions, nil] unless should_process_with_magick?(bytes, image_type)

      tempfile = Tempfile.new(["profile_image", ".#{extension}"], binmode: true)
      tempfile.write(bytes)
      tempfile.flush

      frame_count = 1
      if %i[gif webp].include?(image_type) || !Rails.env.test?
        begin
          frame_count = MiniMagick::Image.new(tempfile.path).frames.count
        rescue Timeout::Error
          return [nil, nil, I18n.t("services.images.profile_image_processor.timeout")]
        end

        if frame_count > FRAME_MAX
          return [
            nil,
            nil,
            I18n.t("services.images.profile_image_processor.too_many_frames", frame_max: FRAME_MAX),
          ]
        end
      end

      begin
        image = MiniMagick::Image.new(tempfile.path)
        image.combine_options do |cmd|
          cmd.auto_orient
          cmd.strip unless frame_count > FRAME_STRIP_MAX
        end
        processed = File.binread(tempfile.path)
        updated_dimensions = FastImage.size(StringIO.new(processed)) || dimensions
        [processed, updated_dimensions, nil]
      rescue StandardError => e
        Rails.logger.error("Error stripping EXIF data from profile image: #{e}")
        [bytes, dimensions, nil]
      end
    ensure
      tempfile&.close!
    end
  end
end
EOF

cat <<'EOF' > app/services/images/remote_profile_image_downloader.rb
require "addressable/uri"
require "net/http"
require "ssrf_filter"
require "uri"

module Images
  # Safely downloads a remote profile image URL with SSRF protection, timeouts,
  # redirect limits, and max-byte-size capping.
  class RemoteProfileImageDownloader
    USER_AGENT = "ForemProfileImageDownloader/1.0".freeze
    OPEN_TIMEOUT = 10
    READ_TIMEOUT = 10
    MAX_REDIRECTS = 5

    class ResponseTooLargeError < StandardError; end

    Result = Struct.new(:success, :bytes, :error, keyword_init: true) do
      def success?
        success == true
      end

      def empty?
        bytes.nil? || bytes.bytesize.zero?
      end

      def self.success(bytes)
        new(success: true, bytes: bytes, error: nil)
      end

      def self.failure(message)
        new(success: false, bytes: nil, error: message)
      end
    end

    def self.skip_ssrf_protection?
      false
    end

    def self.call(url)
      new(url).call
    end

    def initialize(url)
      @url = url.to_s
    end

    def call
      uri = parse_uri(@url)
      bytes = if self.class.skip_ssrf_protection?
                download_without_ssrf_filter(uri)
              else
                download_with_ssrf_filter(uri)
              end

      Result.success(bytes)
    rescue ResponseTooLargeError
      human_max = ActiveSupport::NumberHelper.number_to_human_size(ProfileImageProcessor::MAX_FILE_SIZE)
      Result.failure(I18n.t("services.images.profile_image_processor.max_size_error", max_size: human_max))
    rescue StandardError => e
      Result.failure("#{I18n.t('services.images.remote_profile_image_downloader.download_error')}: #{e.message}")
    end

    private

    def parse_uri(source)
      parsed = Addressable::URI.parse(source)
      unless %w[http https].include?(parsed.scheme&.downcase)
        raise URI::InvalidURIError, "unsupported scheme for #{source}"
      end

      parsed.host = parsed.normalized_host
      URI.parse(parsed.to_s)
    rescue Addressable::URI::InvalidURIError => e
      raise URI::InvalidURIError, e.message
    end

    def download_with_ssrf_filter(uri)
      max_bytes = ProfileImageProcessor::MAX_FILE_SIZE
      body = +"".b

      response = SsrfFilter.get(
        uri,
        headers: { "User-Agent" => USER_AGENT },
        max_redirects: MAX_REDIRECTS,
        http_options: { open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT, read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT },
      ) do |res|
        body = +"".b
        res.read_body do |chunk|
          body << chunk.b
          raise ResponseTooLargeError if body.bytesize > max_bytes
        end
      end

      response.value
      body
    end

    def download_without_ssrf_filter(uri, redirects_left = MAX_REDIRECTS)
      max_bytes = ProfileImageProcessor::MAX_FILE_SIZE

      Net::HTTP.start(
        uri.hostname,
        uri.port,
        use_ssl: uri.scheme == "https",
        open_timeout: OPEN_TIMEOUT,
        read_timeout: READ_TIMEOUT,
      ) do |http|
        request = Net::HTTP::Get.new(uri)
        request["User-Agent"] = USER_AGENT

        body = +"".b
        response = http.request(request) do |res|
          if res.is_a?(Net::HTTPSuccess)
            res.read_body do |chunk|
              body << chunk.b
              raise ResponseTooLargeError if body.bytesize > max_bytes
            end
          end
        end

        if response.is_a?(Net::HTTPRedirection) && redirects_left.positive? && response["location"].present?
          next_uri = parse_uri(URI.join(uri.to_s, response["location"]).to_s)
          return download_without_ssrf_filter(next_uri, redirects_left - 1)
        end

        response.value
        body
      end
    end
  end
end
EOF
